observations: Embedded environment lacks stat; installation uses numeric POSIX ls ownership/mode checks
Embedded sleep rejects fractional seconds; publication lock uses integer-second waits
Official ripgrep version output can include an optional revision suffix
Repair test corrupts managed ripgrep while preserving the original helper executable and live runtime
Upgrade test uses actual helper 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 artifacts, with a live acceptance child and same-runtime reconnect
The unusable default-root test uses an account-owned directory with mode 500 and verifies explicit policy rejection, including for privileged accounts
Partial upload and lost publication response are deterministic control-transport fault injections
limitations: Caller supplies trusted metadata and local cache; no release downloader, signed catalog, public binary/npm distribution or package compatibility claim
No new Rust implementation or 13-group helper rerun in this milestone; helper 0.1.1 artifacts are unchanged from recorded accepted binaries
Forced SIGKILL of publication shell may leave a lock; timeout reports INSTALL_BUSY without unsafe takeover
Unreferenced staging and inactive generations have no automatic garbage collector; peak installation disk usage and power-loss durability were not measured
No hostile same-account/ancestor-path race guarantee; the SSH account remains the permission boundary
Lost initial startup/hello can leave an unbound helper until finite grace and an empty temporary parent
The DSH tests exercise source-based consumers, not creation/resume-time Agent context, approvals, Session jobs, PTY adapter or full application consumers
Linux x86_64 manifest uses conservative glibc 2.39 requirement; minimum general distribution ABI floor remains unmeasured
